weightageNote: Weightage: 4-8% (1-2 guaranteed questions in JEE Mains / NEET UG). Unit 20 Experimental Skills is a top scoring zone.
syllabusAlert: Syllabus Sync: Zero deletions. Vernier Callipers, Screw Gauge, Meter Bridge, Resonance Tube & Error Propagation are retained across all tracks.

sections.heading: SI Base Units, Dimensional Homogeneity & Application Limits
sections.summary: Physical quantities follow dimensional homogeneity: every additive or subtractive term in an equation must carry identical [M^a L^b T^c A^d K^e mol^f cd^g] exponents.
keyPoints: Seven SI base quantities: Mass [M], Length [L], Time [T], Current [I or A], Temperature [K], Amount [mol], Luminous Intensity [cd].
Dimensionless arguments: arguments of sin(x), cos(x), e^x, ln(x), and ratios like strain, refractive index, relative permittivity are strictly [M^0 L^0 T^0].
Energy Density u = (1/2) eps_0 E^2 = B^2 / (2 mu_0) = Pressure = Stress = Young's Modulus = [M L^(-1) T^(-2)].
Time constant benchmarks: RC = L/R = sqrt(LC) = [T]; Stefan constant sigma = [M T^(-3) K^(-4)]; Universal constant R = [M L^2 T^(-2) K^(-1) mol^(-1)].

sections.heading: Significant Figures, Rounding & Limiting Error Propagation
sections.summary: Significant digits convey measurement precision. Always combine absolute errors linearly during addition/subtraction and fractional errors during multiplication/powers.
keyPoints: Exact numbers (2, pi) carry infinite significant digits. Trailing zeros AFTER decimal point ARE significant (4.200 has 4 SF); trailing zeros without decimal (4200) carry only 2 SF.
Sum/Difference (Z = A +/- B): Maximum absolute error dZ = dA + dB (NEVER subtract absolute errors even when Z = A - B).
Product/Quotient/Power (Z = A^p * B^q / C^r): Maximum fractional error dZ/Z = |p|(dA/A) + |q|(dB/B) + |r|(dC/C).
Round final answer to LEAST decimal places (in +/-) or LEAST significant figures (in x or /).

sections.heading: Unit 20 Experimental Instruments: Vernier Callipers & Screw Gauge
sections.summary: Least Count (LC) determines smallest reliably readable scale fraction. Corrected reading always subtracts zero error with its algebraic sign.
keyPoints: Vernier Callipers: LC = 1 MSD - 1 VSD. If n VSD coincide with (n - 1) MSD, then LC = (1 MSD) / n. Observed = MSR + (VSR x LC).
Screw Gauge / Micrometer: Pitch = Linear advancement per full rotation. LC = Pitch / Circular Scale Divisions (N). Typical: Pitch 0.5 mm, N = 50 -> LC = 0.01 mm.
Zero Error Rule: Positive zero error (vernier 0 sits right of main 0, or circular 0 lies below reference line) -> subtract (+e). Negative zero error -> subtract (-|e|), effectively adding |e|.

formulas.note: Applies to Z = k A^p B^q C^(-r); multiply by 100 for % error
When n VSD = (n-1) MSD; True = MSR + VSR*LC - ZeroError
Backlash error avoided by rotating screw in one direction only
End correction e = (L2 - 3*L1)/2 cancels automatically in L2 - L1

comparison.title: Experimental Error & Sign Convention Matrix
rows: +e if 0 of VS is right of 0 of MS
Assuming negative zero error directly equals -k*LC instead of -(n - k)*LC
+e if CS zero sits BELOW datum line
Forgetting to convert mm to cm before plugging into volume/area
Maximum accuracy occurs ONLY near null point l ~= 50 cm
Timing 20 oscillations divides dT/T by 20 vs timing 1 oscillation

traps: In Z = A - B, errors ALWAYS ADD (dZ = dA + dB). Never write dA - dB!
For negative Vernier zero error when 7th VSD coincides (10 VSD = 9 MSD): Zero Error = -(10 - 7) x LC = -3 x LC, NOT -7 x LC!
Standard EMF or Planck h vs Angular Momentum: h has [M L^2 T^(-1)] same as angular momentum L, while Torque has [M L^2 T^(-2)] same as Energy.

solvedExamples.question: In a Screw Gauge, 4 full rotations advance the spindle by 2 mm. The circular scale has 50 divisions. While measuring a wire, MSR = 3 mm, CSR = 32, and zero error = -0.04 mm. Find true diameter.
steps: Observed Reading = 3 mm + 32 x 0.01 mm = 3.32 mm.
True Reading = Observed - Zero Error = 3.32 - (-0.04) = 3.36 mm.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Subtracting +0.04 instead of (-0.04) gives 3.28 mm (classic distractor option).

solvedExamples.question: Given force F = a * t^(-1) + b * t^2, where t is time. Find dimensions of a / b.
steps: By homogeneity: [a * t^(-1)] = [F] => [a] = [M L T^(-2)] * [T] = [M L T^(-1)].
solvedExamples.pitfall: Writing F * t^(-1) instead of multiplying by t when isolating a.

weightageNote: Weightage: 4-6% (1-2 questions across 1D calculus motion, horizontal/inclined projectiles & river-boat problems).
syllabusAlert: Syllabus Sync: Scalar/vector differentiation, parabolic trajectories, inclined projection & relative velocity fully retained.

sections.heading: Calculus Kinematics: Variable Acceleration & Motion Graphs
sections.summary: Instantaneous velocity v = dx/dt and acceleration a = dv/dt = v (dv/dx) handle any non-uniform acceleration problem.
keyPoints: Slope of x-t gives instantaneous velocity; slope of v-t gives acceleration; area under v-t curve gives DISPLACEMENT (algebraic sum) while sum of |area| gives DISTANCE.
Area under a-x graph equals (v^2 - u^2)/2 because integral(a dx) = integral(v dv).
In uniformly accelerated motion starting from rest, distances travelled in equal consecutive time intervals follow Galileo's odd ratio 1 : 3 : 5 : 7...

sections.heading: 2D Projectile Motion & Inclined Plane Projection
sections.summary: Resolve velocity and gravity independently along perpendicular axes. Along horizontal, a_x = 0 so v_x = u cos(theta) stays constant throughout.
keyPoints: Trajectory equation: y = x tan(theta) - (g x^2) / (2 u^2 cos^2(theta)) = x tan(theta) * (1 - x / R).
Horizontal Range R = u^2 sin(2*theta) / g is identical for complementary launch angles theta and (90 deg - theta); H_1 / H_2 = tan^2(theta).
Upward inclined plane (incline angle beta, launch alpha to horizontal): resolve perpendicular (g cos beta) and parallel (-g sin beta) to incline. T = 2u sin(alpha - beta) / (g cos beta).

sections.heading: Relative Motion: River-Boat & Rain-Umbrella Vectors
sections.summary: Relative velocity v_AB = v_A - v_B converts moving-frame scenarios into single-observer geometry.
keyPoints: Minimum time to cross river of width d: steer STRICTLY perpendicular to bank -> t_min = d / v_b (drift = v_r * t_min).
Shortest path (zero drift) requires v_b > v_r: steer upstream at sin(theta) = v_r / v_b from normal -> resultant speed = sqrt(v_b^2 - v_r^2).
Closest approach of two particles: compute relative velocity v_rel, then drop perpendicular d_min = |r_rel x v_rel| / |v_rel|.

formulas.note: Valid ONLY for constant acceleration with zero direction reversal check
Occurs at alpha = pi/4 + beta/2; for flat beta = 0 -> u^2 / g
Independent of river stream velocity v_r
Harmonic mean for equal distances; arithmetic mean (v1+v2)/2 for equal times

traps: Distance >= |Displacement| always. Check if velocity v(t) changes sign inside [t1, t2] before calling displacement equal to distance!
At highest point of projectile, velocity is u cos(theta) horizontally (NOT zero) and speed radius of curvature R_c = u^2 cos^2(theta) / g.
Do not plug angle theta measured from VERTICAL into standard u^2 sin(2*theta)/g blindly without checking complement!

solvedExamples.question: A particle moves along x-axis with v = alpha * sqrt(x). Find acceleration as a function of time starting from rest at x = 0.
steps: dx/dt = alpha * x^(1/2) => integral x^(-1/2) dx = integral alpha dt.
Differentiating twice: v = dx/dt = (alpha^2 * t)/2 and a = dv/dt = alpha^2 / 2 (constant!).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Evaluating v dv/dx gives (alpha*sqrt(x)) * (alpha/(2*sqrt(x))) = alpha^2 / 2 instantly in 1 line!

solvedExamples.question: A projectile has horizontal range R = 4 * sqrt(3) * H_max. Find launch angle theta.
steps: Given R / H = 4 * sqrt(3) => 4 / tan(theta) = 4 * sqrt(3) => tan(theta) = 1 / sqrt(3).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Remember R = 4 H cot(theta); at 45 deg, R = 4H.

weightageNote: Weightage: 4-6% (Pulleys, wedges, friction equilibrium & circular banking).
syllabusAlert: Syllabus Sync: Complete Newton's Laws, Pseudo Force, Static/Kinetic Friction & Circular Dynamics retained.

sections.heading: Constraint Relations, Pulley-Block FBDs & Pseudo Force
sections.summary: Virtual work theorem Sum(T . a) = 0 solves any complex movable-pulley acceleration constraint immediately without differentiating rope lengths manually.
keyPoints: Draw isolated Free Body Diagrams (FBDs) including Weight, Normal N, Tension T, Spring kx, and Friction f.
Pseudo Force F_p = -m * a_frame must be applied OPPOSITE to frame acceleration whenever solving inside an accelerating elevator, trolley, or wedge.
Ideal spring cannot change tension instantaneously when a connected string is cut, whereas massless inextensible string tension adjusts immediately.

sections.heading: Static vs Kinetic Friction & Two-Block Systems
sections.summary: Static friction is self-adjusting (0 <= f_s <= mu_s N) whereas kinetic friction assumes a constant value f_k = mu_k N opposing relative slip.
keyPoints: Angle of Repose theta_r = arctan(mu_s): inclination at which block just starts sliding down.
Minimum pulling force to slide block on rough flat surface equals mu * m * g / sqrt(1 + mu^2) applied upward at angle theta = arctan(mu).
Two-block stack trick: assume both move together with common acceleration a_c; check if required f <= mu_s N_top; if exceeded, blocks slip separately.

sections.heading: Circular Dynamics & Conical Pendulum
sections.summary: Centripetal force m v^2 / r = m omega^2 r points radially INWARD and performs zero work in circular motion.
keyPoints: Safe turn on rough flat road: v_max = sqrt(mu g r). Ideal frictionless banked road: tan(theta) = v^2 / (r g).
Combined banked + rough road maximum speed: v_max = sqrt( r g (sin theta + mu cos theta) / (cos theta - mu sin theta) ).
Conical pendulum period: T = 2 * pi * sqrt( (L cos theta) / g ).

formulas.note: Instantaneous constraint for interconnected movable pulleys
Zero lateral tire friction needed at this exact speed
Horizontal wedge acceleration a = g tan theta keeps block at rest on wedge

comparison.title: Spring-Cut vs String-Cut Instantaneous Dynamics
rows: Spring force kx STAYS unchanged at t = 0+
Cut string T -> 0 immediately; jump acceleration a = kx/m

traps: Static friction is NOT fixed at mu_s N; it only equals the driving force until slipping begins!
At high speed on banked road with friction, check whether v > sqrt(rg tan theta) (friction points DOWN incline) or v < sqrt(rg tan theta) (friction points UP incline).

solvedExamples.question: A 2 kg block sits on a 4 kg lower block (smooth floor). Friction between blocks has mu = 0.4. Find maximum horizontal force F on lower 4 kg block so both move together (g = 10 m/s^2).
steps: Max friction driving top 2 kg block = f_max = 0.4 x 2 x 10 = 8 N.
Max acceleration top block can sustain = 8 / 2 = 4 m/s^2.
Apply F = (M + m) a_max = (4 + 2) x 4 = 24 N.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Applying F directly to top block gives a different F_max = (m+M) * (f_max / M) = 6 x (8/4) = 12 N!

weightageNote: Weightage: 5-7% (Work-Energy Theorem, Vertical Circles, Potential Wells & 1D/2D Collisions).
syllabusAlert: Syllabus Sync: All WEP, Centre of Mass & Restitution Collision concepts retained.

sections.heading: Work-Energy Theorem & Conservative Force Potential Wells
sections.summary: W_total = W_conservative + W_non-conservative + W_ext = Delta K holds universally in inertial AND non-inertial frames (including work by pseudo force).
keyPoints: Conservative force: F = -dU/dx (in 3D: F = -grad U). Mechanical energy K + U stays conserved ONLY when non-conservative & external forces do zero work.
Equilibrium occurs where dU/dx = 0: Stable (d^2U/dx^2 > 0, potential minimum), Unstable (d^2U/dx^2 < 0, max), Neutral (d^2U/dx^2 = 0).

sections.heading: Vertical Circular Motion (Looping the Loop)
sections.summary: Minimum critical speeds prevent string slackening at top of vertical circle.
keyPoints: Mass on string of length L: min speed at bottom = sqrt(5 g L) -> top speed = sqrt(g L), T_top = 0, T_bottom = 6 m g.
T_bottom - T_top = 6 m g identically for ANY looping speed above critical threshold.
Mass on massless rigid rod or inside double track: min bottom speed drops to sqrt(4 g L) because rod supports zero speed at top!

sections.heading: Centre of Mass & Newton Restitution Collisions
sections.summary: With zero external net impulse, total linear momentum P and COM velocity remain invariant through any collision or explosion.
keyPoints: Coefficient of restitution e = (v2 - v1)_sep / (u1 - u2)_app along Line of Impact. Elastic e = 1, Perfectly Inelastic e = 0.
1D elastic collision between equal masses swaps velocities identically.
Perfectly inelastic head-on loss of KE: Delta K = (1/2) * [m1 m2 / (m1 + m2)] * (u1 - u2)^2 * (1 - e^2).

formulas.note: Holds for constant, variable, friction & spring forces universally
If sqrt(2gL) < v_bottom < sqrt(5gL), string slackens above horizontal
Two equal smooth spheres separate perpendicularly after oblique e=1 impact

comparison.title: Collision Classification & Energy Retention
rows: Bodies stick together; max allowed KE loss

traps: Work by static friction CAN be non-zero in ground frame (e.g. block accelerating on moving truck), though total static-friction work across both surfaces together cancels to zero!
For bouncing ball from height h_0 with restitution e: rebound height h_n = e^(2n) * h_0, total distance = h_0 * (1 + e^2)/(1 - e^2).

solvedExamples.question: A ball drops from 16 m onto a horizontal floor and rebounds to 9 m. Compute coefficient of restitution e and height after 2nd bounce.
steps: Speed before impact = sqrt(2gh1), after impact = sqrt(2gh2).
Height after 2nd bounce = h1 * e^4 = 16 x (9/16)^2 = 81/16 = 5.0625 m.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using h2/h1 instead of sqrt(h2/h1) gives wrong e = 9/16.

weightageNote: Weightage: 6-8% (Highest-yield Mechanics chapter across JEE Mains, JEE Advanced & NEET).
syllabusAlert: Syllabus Sync: Parallel/Perpendicular Axes Theorems, Torque, Pure Rolling & Angular Momentum Conservation fully retained.

sections.heading: Moment of Inertia (MOI) & Axis Theorems
sections.summary: Rotational analogue of mass depends directly on mass distribution relative to rotation axis: I = Sum m_i r_i^2.
keyPoints: Parallel Axis Theorem (any 3D body): I = I_cm + M d^2 (I_cm MUST pass through Centre of Mass!).
Perpendicular Axis Theorem (PLANAR laminae ONLY): I_z = I_x + I_y where x, y lie in lamina plane and z is normal.
Standard I_cm (k^2/R^2): Ring = MR^2 (1), Disc/Solid Cylinder = MR^2/2 (1/2), Hollow Sphere = 2/3 MR^2 (2/3), Solid Sphere = 2/5 MR^2 (2/5), Rod(centre) = ML^2/12.

sections.heading: Pure Rolling & Rolling Down an Inclined Plane
sections.summary: Zero slip at bottom contact enforces v_cm = omega R and a_cm = alpha R, making bottom point the Instantaneous Centre of Rotation (ICOR).
keyPoints: Rolling acceleration down incline angle theta: a = g sin(theta) / (1 + I_cm / (M R^2)). Solid sphere always wins race against disc, hollow sphere, and ring!
Minimum static friction for pure rolling down incline: mu_min = tan(theta) / (1 + M R^2 / I_cm).
Total Rolling KE = (1/2) m v_cm^2 [1 + k^2/R^2] = translational KE + rotational KE.

sections.heading: Angular Momentum Conservation & Frictional Impulse
sections.summary: When net external torque about point O vanishes (tau_O = 0), angular momentum L_O = I_cm omega + r_cm x (m v_cm) stays conserved.
keyPoints: Toppling condition of cube (side a) on rough ramp: block topples BEFORE sliding if tan(theta) > 1 when mu > 1.
Point mass hitting pivoted rod or free rod: conserve L about hinge (eliminates hinge impulse!) or about line of impact.

formulas.note: Sphere (5/7 g sin theta) > Disc (2/3) > Hollow Sphere (3/5) > Ring (1/2)

formulas.formula: L_O = I_cm * omega + M (r_cm x v_cm)
formulas.note: Orbital + spin term both required for moving bodies
For ring = (tan theta)/2; solid sphere = (2/7) tan theta

comparison.title: Rolling Rigid Body Parameters (Radius R, Mass M)

traps: Perpendicular Axis Theorem I_z = I_x + I_y CANNOT be used for 3D solid spheres or solid cylinders!
In Parallel Axis Theorem I = I_cm + Md^2, I_cm MUST pass through the Centre of Mass — never jump between two non-COM axes directly!
During pure rolling on flat ground at constant speed, static friction is ZERO!

solvedExamples.question: A solid sphere of mass 5 kg rolls without slipping at 10 m/s. Find its total kinetic energy and rotational fraction.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Calculating only (1/2)Mv^2 = 250 J forgets the 100 J rotational KE!

weightageNote: Weightage: 3-4% (High ROI! Direct formula parallels with Electrostatics).
syllabusAlert: Syllabus Sync: Shell theorem, variation of g, escape/orbital speed & Kepler's 3 laws fully retained.

sections.heading: Gravitational Field, Potential & Gauss Shell Analogues
sections.summary: Gravitational field is conservative (E = -dV/dr). Uniform solid sphere inside field increases linearly with r, whereas hollow shell inside field is strictly zero.
keyPoints: Hollow spherical shell: E_in = 0, V_in = -GM/R (constant); outside E = GM/r^2, V = -GM/r.
Solid uniform sphere: E_in = GMr / R^3; V_in = -GM(3R^2 - r^2) / (2 R^3). At centre, V_centre = 1.5 x V_surface = -3GM/(2R).
Uniform circular ring on axis (x): E = GMx / (R^2 + x^2)^(3/2), maximum at x = R/sqrt(2).

sections.heading: Variation of g, Escape Velocity & Satellite Mechanics
sections.summary: Gravity decreases with both altitude h and depth d below Earth surface, peaking right on the surface.
keyPoints: Height h: g' = g / (1 + h/R)^2 ~= g(1 - 2h/R) for h << R. Depth d: g' = g(1 - d/R) exact for uniform sphere.
Escape velocity v_e = sqrt(2GM/R) = sqrt(2gR) ~= 11.2 km/s (independent of projectile mass & launch angle!).
Circular satellite orbit: v_o = sqrt(GM/r) = v_e / sqrt(2) (at surface), KE = +GMm/(2r), PE = -GMm/r, Total E = -GMm/(2r) = -KE.
Kepler 2nd Law (dA/dt = L/(2m) = constant) = Angular Momentum Conservation; 3rd Law: T^2 proportional to a^3.

formulas.note: Binding energy BE = |E| = +GMm/(2r)
Identical to near-surface orbiting satellite time period!
Reduced mass mu orbits common COM separated by distance d

traps: Using approximate g(1 - 2h/R) when h = R/2 or h = R fails badly! Always use exact g/(1 + h/R)^2 unless h << R.
Geostationary satellite has fixed T = 24 hours (~36,000 km altitude), equatorial plane, West-to-East sense.

solvedExamples.question: At what height h above Earth's surface (radius R) does acceleration due to gravity drop to g/4?
steps: Taking square roots: 1 + h/R = 2 => h = R.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using binomial (1 - 2h/R) = 1/4 wrongly predicts h = 3R/8!

weightageNote: Weightage: 4-5% (Elasticity Thermal Stress, Hydrostatics, Bernoulli Efflux & Surface Tension Excess Pressure).
syllabusAlert: Syllabus Sync: Stress-Strain, Pascal/Archimedes, Bernoulli, Stokes Viscosity & Capillarity all retained.

sections.heading: Elasticity, Elastic Energy Density & Thermal Stress
sections.summary: Young's modulus Y = stress/strain measures stiffness of solids; clamped rods develop thermal stress sigma = Y * alpha * Delta T when temperature changes.
keyPoints: Elongation under force F: dL = FL / (AY). Under own weight W: dL = WL / (2AY) (half as much!).
Elastic potential energy density u = (1/2) stress x strain = sigma^2 / (2Y) = (1/2) Y (strain)^2.

sections.heading: Fluid Mechanics: Buoyancy, Continuity & Bernoulli
sections.summary: Incompressible steady streamline flow conserves A*v = constant and energy P + (1/2) rho v^2 + rho g h = constant.
keyPoints: Torricelli efflux speed from hole depth h: v = sqrt(2gh); range on ground R = 2 sqrt(h(H - h)), maximized at h = H/2 giving R_max = H.
In accelerating container (a horizontally), free fluid surface tilts at tan(theta) = a / g perpendicular to g_eff.

sections.heading: Viscosity (Stokes' Law) & Surface Tension / Capillarity
sections.summary: Surface tension S minimizes liquid area (W = S * Delta A); viscous drag opposes motion through fluids.
keyPoints: Stokes drag F = 6 pi eta r v; terminal speed v_T = 2 r^2 (rho_s - rho_l) g / (9 eta) proportional to r^2.
Excess pressure: Liquid drop = 2S/R; Soap bubble in air = 4S/R (two interfaces!). Coalescing N drops -> U_final / U_initial = N^(-1/3).
Capillary ascent (Jurin's Law): h = 2 S cos(theta) / (r rho g); inadequate length tube never overflows — meniscus radius flattens instead!

formulas.note: Independent of rod length L; F = Y A alpha Delta T
8 identical rain drops coalescing multiply terminal speed by 4!

formulas.formula: h = (2 S cos theta) / (r rho g)
formulas.note: h * r = constant for tube of insufficient height

comparison.title: Excess Pressure & Surface Energy Reference
rows: Air Bubble Inside Water / Liquid Drop
2 * S * (4 pi R^2) = 8 pi R^2 S

traps: Always multiply area change by 2 for soap films and soap bubbles in air!
If capillary tube is tilted at angle alpha to vertical, vertical height h stays constant while slanted water column length increases to h / cos(alpha).

solvedExamples.question: Work done to blow a soap bubble of radius R is W. Additional work needed to double its radius from R to 2R is:
steps: Initial energy W = 2 x S x 4 pi R^2 = 8 pi R^2 S.
At radius 2R, total energy = 8 pi (2R)^2 S = 4 W.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Returning 4W gives total work from zero radius, forgetting initial W already done.

weightageNote: Weightage: 6-8% (High-yield block across JEE Mains, NEET & IIT Adv).
syllabusAlert: Syllabus Sync: NTA JEE Mains dropped Carnot Engine/Heat Pump, which REMAIN in JEE Advanced [ADV ONLY] (phy_adv2). Conduction, Stefan/Wien Radiation, KTG & 1st Law are core everywhere.

sections.heading: Thermal Expansion, Conduction & Radiation Laws
sections.summary: Linear beta = 2*alpha, volumetric gamma = 3*alpha; heat conduction obeys thermal Ohm's law R_th = L / (k A).
keyPoints: Conduction steady state rate: dQ/dt = k A Delta T / L = Delta T / R_th. Series rods add R_th; parallel add 1/R_th.
Wien's Displacement Law: lambda_max * T = b ~= 2.898 x 10^(-3) m.K (blue star hotter than red star).
Stefan-Boltzmann Law: Radiated power P = e sigma A T^4; net rate in surroundings T_0 is e sigma A (T^4 - T_0^4).

sections.heading: Kinetic Theory of Gases (KTG) & Equipartition
sections.summary: Ideal gas molecules carry (f/2) k_B T average kinetic energy per degree of freedom f.
keyPoints: f = 3 (monoatomic), 5 (diatomic/linear rigid at room T), 6 (non-linear polyatomic). C_v = f R / 2, C_p = C_v + R, gamma = 1 + 2/f.
Speed hierarchy: v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M) > v_avg = sqrt(8RT / (pi M)) > v_mp = sqrt(2RT/M) => ratio sqrt(3) : sqrt(8/pi) : sqrt(2).
Gas Mixture: n_mix C_v_mix = n1 C_v1 + n2 C_v2.

sections.heading: First Law of Thermodynamics & Molar Heat Capacities
sections.summary: dQ = dU + dW holds universally with dU = n C_v dT depending ONLY on temperature for ideal gases.
keyPoints: Sign convention (Physics): +dQ absorbed by gas, +dW = P dV expansion work BY gas, +dU rise in T.
Isothermal (T=const): dU=0, Q=W = nRT ln(V2/V1); Adiabatic (Q=0): P V^gamma = const, W = nR(T1 - T2)/(gamma - 1).
Polytropic P V^x = const: Molar heat capacity C = C_v + R / (1 - x). Slope of adiabatic on P-V is gamma times steeper than isothermal!

formulas.formula: dU = n C_v dT ; C_p - C_v = R
formulas.note: Always valid for ALL ideal gas processes (even irreversible!)
For P V^x = const; negative C implies T drops while Q enters
Solid vs hollow sphere same mass -> hollow cools slower? Same area -> equal P, same mass -> equal dT/dt; equal R -> hollow cools faster!

traps: Always insert Kelvin T into PV=nRT, Stefan T^4, Wien lambda*T, and RMS speeds — NEVER Celsius!
In a cyclic process, total dU_cycle = 0, so Q_net = W_net = enclosed PV loop area (CW loop = positive net work!).

solvedExamples.question: 1 mole monoatomic (He) and 1 mole diatomic (N2) ideal gas mix at T. Compute effective gamma_mix.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Never average gamma1 and gamma2 linearly! Always average n * C_v.

weightageNote: Weightage: 4-5% (SHM Phase/Springs, Progressive Waves, Standing Strings & Organ Pipes).
syllabusAlert: Syllabus Sync: Doppler Effect removed from NTA JEE Mains (retained in JEE Adv [ADV ONLY] phy_adv2). SHM, Superposition, Beats & Resonance Pipes core across all exams.

sections.heading: Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM) & Spring Systems
sections.summary: Restoring acceleration a = -omega^2 x drives sinusoidal motion x = A sin(omega t + phi).
keyPoints: Velocity v = omega sqrt(A^2 - x^2); v_max = omega A at mean x=0; a_max = omega^2 A at extremes x=+/-A.
Total Energy E = (1/2) m omega^2 A^2; KE = PE identically when x = +/- A / sqrt(2).
Spring constants: Parallel k_eq = k1 + k2; Series 1/k_eq = 1/k1 + 1/k2; Reduced mass mu = m1*m2/(m1+m2) for two-body spring oscillation.

sections.heading: Mechanical Waves, Standing Waves & Beats
sections.summary: Transverse wave speed on string v = sqrt(T/mu). Superposition of identical counter-propagating waves forms stationary nodes/antinodes.
keyPoints: Adjacent node-to-node or antinode-to-antinode spacing = lambda / 2; node-to-antinode = lambda / 4.
Open Organ Pipe (antinodes both ends): ALL harmonics present, f_n = n v / (2 L) (n = 1, 2, 3...).
Closed Organ Pipe (one closed node, one open antinode): ONLY ODD harmonics present, f_n = (2n - 1) v / (4 L).
Beat frequency f_beat = |f1 - f2|. Filing tuning fork slightly INCREASES frequency; loading with wax DECREASES frequency.

formulas.formula: T_spring = 2 pi sqrt(m/k) ; T_pendulum = 2 pi sqrt(L/g_eff)
formulas.note: In freely falling lift g_eff = 0 => pendulum never oscillates (T -> infinity)

formulas.formula: T = 2 pi sqrt(mu / k), mu = m1*m2/(m1+m2)
formulas.note: Both blocks oscillate in opposite phase
Fundamental open frequency = 2 x closed frequency of equal length L

traps: Remember a displacement NODE in a sound wave is simultaneously a PRESSURE ANTINODE!
If amplitude is A, phase angle from mean to A/2 takes T/12, whereas from A/2 to A takes T/6 (twice as long because it slows down!).

solvedExamples.question: A tuning fork A gives 4 beats/s with a 256 Hz fork B. On filing fork A slightly, beat frequency rises to 6 beats/s. Find original frequency of A.
steps: Filing reduces mass and INCREASES frequency of A.
Since beat gap widened from 4 to 6, A must already be above 256 (rising 260 -> 262 gives 6 beats; rising 252 -> 254 would drop beats to 2).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Filing INCREASES f; waxing DECREASES f.

weightageNote: Weightage: 7-9% (Highest-weightage Class 12 block: Gauss Law, Dipole, Conductors & RC Capacitors).

sections.heading: Electric Field, Dipoles & Gauss's Law Flux Symmetry
sections.summary: Gauss Law Flux Phi = q_enclosed / eps_0 counts strictly charges inside the closed Gaussian surface, though E on surface includes all charges.
keyPoints: Dipole field: Axial E = 2kp/r^3 (parallel to p); Equatorial E = kp/r^3 (anti-parallel to p). Torque tau = p x E, Energy U = -p . E.
Gaussian cube symmetry: charge q at centre -> q/(6 eps_0) per face; at face centre -> q/(2 eps_0) through cube; at corner -> q/(8 eps_0) through cube.
Conducting spheres: charge stays strictly on outer surfaces; field inside bulk conductor = 0; surface force pressure = sigma^2 / (2 eps_0).

sections.heading: Potential, Earthing & Capacitors with Dielectrics / RC Loops
sections.summary: Parallel plate capacitance C = K eps_0 A / d stores electrostatic energy U = (1/2) C V^2 = Q^2 / (2C).
keyPoints: Battery DISCONNECTED while inserting dielectric K: Q stays constant -> E/K, V/K, C->KC, U->U/K.
Battery CONNECTED while inserting dielectric K: V stays constant -> E unchanged, Q->KQ, C->KC, U->KU (battery supplies work!).
Partial slab thickness t (dielectric K): C = eps_0 A / (d - t + t/K). RC charging time constant tau = R_eq * C.

formulas.note: Work needed to assemble charge from infinity

formulas.formula: q(t) = C V (1 - e^(-t / R_eq C))
formulas.note: At t=0 uncharged capacitor = short wire; at t=infinity = open switch
Heat loss dH = 1/2 [C1 C2 / (C1 + C2)] (V1 - V2)^2

traps: Connecting charged capacitor C to identical uncharged C dissipates EXACTLY 50% of initial energy as spark heat!
Always find R_eq across capacitor terminals AFTER shorting all ideal DC batteries to calculate time constant tau = R_eq C!

solvedExamples.question: A dielectric slab (K = 4) fills half the gap thickness (t = d/2) inside an isolated parallel plate capacitor C_0 = 12 uF. Find new capacitance.
steps: Effective air gap d_eff = (d - d/2) + (d/2)/4 = d/2 + d/8 = 5d/8.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Treating half-thickness slab in series vs half-area slab in parallel: gap split = SERIES, plate-area split = PARALLEL!

weightageNote: Weightage: 5-7% (Ohm's Law, KCL/KVL, Symmetry Circuits, Meter Bridge & Galvanometer Shunts).

sections.heading: Drift Velocity, Resistance & Symmetric Networks
sections.summary: Current I = n e A v_d with resistivity rho depending solely on material & temperature (independent of wire shape).
keyPoints: Stretching/drawing wire conserving volume: R proportional to L^2 proportional to 1/A^2 proportional to 1/r^4.
Power rating: Bulbs rated P at fixed V have R = V^2 / P -> in SERIES, lowest-wattage bulb glows brightest (I^2 R); in PARALLEL, highest-wattage glows brightest (V^2/R).
Use Folding/Mirror Symmetry to identify equipotential nodes and simplify cube/ladder resistor grids.

sections.heading: Wheatstone Bridge, Meter Bridge & Meter Conversions
sections.summary: Balanced bridge (R1/R2 = R3/R4) passes zero current through galvanometer.
keyPoints: Meter Bridge null point l: X / R = l / (100 - l) (shift happens toward higher resistance end).
Ammeter Conversion: connect TINY shunt S = I_g G / (I - I_g) in PARALLEL. Ideal ammeter R = 0.
Voltmeter Conversion: connect LARGE multiplier R_s = (V / I_g) - G in SERIES. Ideal voltmeter R = infinity.

formulas.note: Check polarity signs strictly when terminals oppose

formulas.formula: P_max = E^2 / (4 r) when R_load = r
formulas.note: Efficiency at max power transfer is strictly 50%

formulas.formula: S = I_g G / (I - I_g) ; R_v = V/I_g - G
formulas.note: Parallel shunt increases range; series multiplier reads higher V

comparison.title: Electrical Measuring Instruments Summary
rows: Low Shunt S in Parallel with G
High R_v in Series with G

traps: 10% stretch in wire length makes L' = 1.1 L -> R' = (1.1)^2 R = 1.21 R (21% increase, NOT 10%!). Never use 2*dL/L approximation for >5% changes.
Reversing one battery terminal reverses its E_i/r_i sign inside the parallel EMF numerator!

solvedExamples.question: A galvanometer of resistance 50 Ohm gives full-scale deflection for 10 mA. How do you convert it to read up to 5 A?
steps: Required shunt S in parallel = (I_g G) / (I - I_g).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Connecting 0.1 Ohm in series destroys deflection and reads wrong current.

sections.heading: Biot-Savart Law & Ampere's Circuital Law
sections.summary: Magnetic field dB = (mu_0 I / 4 pi) (dl x r) / r^3 circulates perpendicular to both wire segment and displacement vector.
keyPoints: Finite wire at perpendicular distance d spanning angles theta_1, theta_2: B = (mu_0 I / 4 pi d)(sin theta_1 + sin theta_2).
Circular arc subtending angle alpha at centre: B = (mu_0 I alpha) / (4 pi R). Solenoid interior: B = mu_0 n I (end = mu_0 n I / 2).
Solid cylinder carrying uniform current density J: B_inside = (mu_0 J r) / 2 proportional to r; outside proportional to 1/r.

sections.heading: Lorentz Force, Helical Paths & Magnetic Materials
sections.summary: Magnetic force F = q(v x B) is always perpendicular to velocity -> does ZERO work and preserves particle speed!
keyPoints: Helical trajectory: radius R = (m v sin theta) / (q B); Time period T = (2 pi m) / (q B) (independent of speed!); Pitch p = (v cos theta) * T.
Parallel currents attract; anti-parallel currents repel with force/length = (mu_0 I1 I2) / (2 pi d).
Dia (chi < 0, weakly repelled), Para (chi > 0 ~ 1/T Curie Law), Ferro (chi >> 1, domains, Curie temperature T_c -> paramagnetic above T_c).

formulas.formula: r = m v / (q B) = sqrt(2 m K) / (q B) = p / (q B)
formulas.note: Equal momentum implies equal radius for same charge q

formulas.formula: tau = M x B ; U = -M . B
formulas.note: Current loop dipole M = N I A

formulas.formula: I_s = NAB / k ; V_s = NAB / (k R)
formulas.note: Doubling turns N doubles I_s but keeps V_s unchanged because R also doubles

traps: Speed & KE NEVER change inside a pure magnetic field (though momentum direction turns)!
Proton (m, q) vs Alpha (4m, 2q) with equal KE -> r = sqrt(2mK)/(qB) -> r_alpha / r_proton = sqrt(4)/2 = 1 : 1 EQUAL radii!

solvedExamples.question: A proton, deuteron (2m, q) and alpha particle (4m, 2q) enter uniform B perpendicularly with EQUAL kinetic energy. Find ratio of circular radii r_p : r_d : r_alpha.
steps: Radius r = sqrt(2 m K) / (q B) => r proportional to sqrt(m) / q.
r_p ~ sqrt(1)/1 = 1; r_d ~ sqrt(2)/1 = sqrt(2); r_alpha ~ sqrt(4)/2 = 1.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Equal KE vs Equal Speed vs Equal Accelerating Potential V give three completely different ratios!

weightageNote: Weightage: 6-8% (Faraday/Lenz Law, Motional EMF, LR Growth, AC LCR Resonance & EM Wave Spectrum).

sections.heading: Faraday's Law, Lenz's Law & Motional EMF
sections.summary: Induced EMF e = -dPhi/dt opposes the change in magnetic flux causing it (energy conservation).
keyPoints: Induced charge flowing through loop R: q_induced = |Delta Phi| / R (completely independent of how fast flux changed!).
Motional EMF across moving rod: e = (v x B) . L. Rotating rod (length L, omega) about one end: e = (1/2) B omega L^2.
Inductor energy U = (1/2) L I^2; LR growth I(t) = (E/R)(1 - e^(-t / tau)) with tau = L / R.

sections.heading: Alternating Current (Series LCR) & EM Waves
sections.summary: RMS current I_rms = I_0 / sqrt(2) produces identical heating to steady DC; average over full cycle is 0, half-cycle = 2 I_0 / pi.
keyPoints: Series LCR Impedance Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2); Phase angle tan(phi) = (X_L - X_C) / R.
Resonance occurs at omega_0 = 1 / sqrt(LC) -> X_L = X_C, Z_min = R, Power Factor cos(phi) = 1 (purely resistive!).
EM Waves: E perpendicular B perpendicular c; E_0 / B_0 = c = 1 / sqrt(mu_0 eps_0); energy split 50% Electric + 50% Magnetic. Wavelength order: Radio > Micro > IR > Vis > UV > X-ray > Gamma.

formulas.formula: P_avg = V_rms I_rms cos(phi) = I_rms^2 R
formulas.note: Pure L or pure C draws strictly zero average wattless power (phi = 90 deg)

formulas.formula: V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p = I_p / I_s (ideal)
formulas.note: Works ONLY with AC (never steady DC!)
Equals conduction current in charging capacitor wires

traps: Remember RMS = Peak / sqrt(2) applies ONLY to sinusoidal/cosinusoidal waves; if I = I_1 + I_2 sin(omega t), then I_rms = sqrt(I_1^2 + I_2^2 / 2)!
At series LCR resonance, V_L and V_C can individually EXCEED source V_applied while cancelling each other 180 deg out of phase!

solvedExamples.question: A 2 m metal rod rotates at 50 rad/s about one end inside perpendicular B = 0.4 T. Find EMF between midpoint and outer end.
steps: EMF between r1 and r2 = (1/2) B omega (r2^2 - r1^2).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using full (1/2) B omega L^2 = 40 V ignores the inner 1 m segment contribution!

weightageNote: Weightage: 7-9% (Mirrors, Refraction, Prisms, Optical Instruments, YDSE & Polarization).

sections.heading: Mirrors, Snell's Law, TIR & Prisms
sections.summary: Cartesian sign convention measures ALL distances from pole/optical centre along incident light direction as positive.
keyPoints: Mirror: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f; m = -v/u = f/(f - u). Lens: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f; m = v/u.
Lens Maker Formula: 1/f = (mu_rel - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2). Immersing glass lens (mu = 1.5) in denser CS2 (mu = 1.65) REVERSES converging/diverging nature!
Prism deviation delta = i + e - A; at minimum deviation i = e and r1 = r2 = A/2 => mu = sin((A + delta_m)/2) / sin(A/2). Thin prism delta = (mu - 1)A.

sections.heading: Wave Optics: YDSE, Diffraction & Polarization
sections.summary: Coherent waves produce bright fringes when path difference Delta x = n lambda and dark fringes when (2n - 1) lambda / 2.
keyPoints: YDSE fringe width beta = lambda D / d. Placing transparent slab (t, mu) shifts fringe pattern by (mu - 1)t * (beta / lambda) toward that slit.
Intensity ratio: I_max / I_min = (sqrt(I1) + sqrt(I2))^2 / (sqrt(I1) - sqrt(I2))^2. For equal I_0: I = 4 I_0 cos^2(phi/2).
Single-slit diffraction MINIMA at a sin(theta) = n lambda; Central maximum angular width = 2 lambda / a. Brewster Law: tan(theta_B) = mu (reflected & refracted rays are 90 deg apart!).

formulas.note: Acts as a mirror with f_eq = -1 / P_eq
Unpolarized light passing first polarizer drops to I_0 / 2 BEFORE Malus cosine factor applies
Normal adjustment relaxed eye drops the '1 +' factor

comparison.title: YDSE Interference vs Single-Slit Diffraction
rows: All fringes equal width beta = lambda D/d

traps: Unpolarized light of intensity I_0 passing through TWO polarizers at angle 60 deg emerges as (I_0 / 2) cos^2(60 deg) = I_0 / 8 (do NOT forget the initial 1/2!).
CRITICAL ANGLE sin(i_c) = mu_rarer / mu_denser; TIR happens ONLY when ray travels from DENSER to RARER medium at i > i_c.

solvedExamples.question: A thin convex glass lens (mu_g = 1.5) has focal length +20 cm in air. Find its focal length when submerged in water (mu_w = 4/3).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Remember convex lens focal length in water (~1.33) becomes ~4x its air focal length!

sections.heading: Photoelectric Effect & Matter Waves (de Broglie)
sections.summary: Photon energy E = hc / lambda ~= 12400 eV.A / lambda(A) transfers in all-or-nothing single electron collisions.
keyPoints: Einstein Photoelectric Equation: K_max = e V_s = h nu - Phi = hc/lambda - hc/lambda_0.
Stopping potential V_s & K_max depend STRICTLY on frequency and work function (independent of light intensity); saturation photocurrent depends on intensity.
de Broglie wavelength lambda = h/p = h / sqrt(2mK). For electron accelerated through V volts: lambda(A) = 12.27 / sqrt(V).

sections.heading: Bohr Atom, Nuclear Binding Energy & Logic Gates
sections.summary: Hydrogen quantized orbits scale as r_n proportional to n^2/Z and energy E_n = -13.6 Z^2 / n^2 eV.
keyPoints: Spectral transitions n2 -> n1 emit max (n2 - n1)(n2 - n1 + 1)/2 distinct lines; Lyman (UV -> n=1), Balmer (Visible -> n=2), Paschen (IR -> n=3).
Nuclear density ~= 2.3 x 10^17 kg/m^3 is CONSTANT for ALL nuclei (R = R_0 A^(1/3)). Reaction Q-value = BE_products - BE_reactants = Delta m x 931.5 MeV.
Semiconductors: Zener diode operates in REVERSE breakdown as voltage regulator; Logic Gates: NAND & NOR are universal gates! De Morgan: (A+B)' = A'.B' and (A.B)' = A' + B'.

formulas.note: Use hc ~= 1240 eV.nm or 12400 eV.A for fast calculations
KE = |E_n| = -U_n / 2 identically
Parallel decay: lambda_eff = lambda1 + lambda2

comparison.title: Boolean Logic Gates Truth Summary
rows: ONLY when BOTH A=1 and B=1
Whenever AT LEAST ONE input is 1
1 ONLY when BOTH A=0 and B=0

traps: Increasing intensity NEVER ejects photoelectrons if incident frequency nu < threshold nu_0!
A p-n junction depletion barrier widens under REVERSE bias and narrows under FORWARD bias; Zener breakdown regulates voltage strictly in REVERSE bias.

solvedExamples.question: Light of wavelength 310 nm strikes a metal of work function 2.0 eV (hc = 1240 eV.nm). Find stopping potential V_s.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Remember stopping potential V_s in Volts numerically equals K_max in eV!

sections.heading: Instantaneous Centre of Rotation (ICOR) & Plank Rolling
sections.summary: For planar rigid body motion, the unique point with zero instantaneous velocity acts as pure rotation pivot: v_P = omega x r_(P/ICOR).
keyPoints: Wheel pure rolling at v_cm = omega R: ICOR sits at bottommost ground contact point; top moves at 2 v_cm, side points move at sqrt(2) v_cm.
Pure rolling on accelerating plank (a_0): constraint enforces a_cm - alpha R = a_0.
Sliding-to-rolling transition: kinetic friction accelerates/decelerates v_cm and changes omega until v_cm = omega R; conserve angular momentum L_ground about stationary ground line throughout!

sections.heading: Variable Mass & Rocket Propulsion
sections.summary: General Newton equation for open mass-changing system: M(dv/dt) = F_ext + v_rel (dm/dt), where v_rel = v_exhaust - v_rocket.
keyPoints: Rocket thrust force F_thrust = |v_rel| (-dm/dt) acts opposite to exhaust ejection.
Gravity-free velocity equation: v = v_0 + v_rel * ln(M_0 / M). Under uniform g: v = v_0 - g t + v_rel * ln(M_0 / M).
Hovering minimum burn rate: (-dm/dt)_min = M g / v_rel.

formulas.formula: v(t) = v_0 - g t + u_rel ln(M_0 / M(t))
formulas.note: u_rel is constant exhaust speed relative to rocket

formulas.formula: Integral(tau_O dt) = L_f - L_i = I Delta omega
formulas.note: Conserve L about contact line to bypass unknown friction impulse

formulas.formula: a_0(max) = mu g (1 + M R^2 / I_cm)
formulas.note: Solid sphere: (7/2) mu g; solid cylinder: 3 mu g

comparison.title: Rolling Transition Conservation Summary
rows: Ball spun & dropped on rough floor
YES (friction line passes through ground pivot!)
Elastic rod-particle impact on smooth table
YES about any fixed table point

traps: Angular momentum about a point P fixed on an ACCELERATING plank is NOT conserved without including pseudo torque -M (r_cm x a_plank)!
At bottom contact of pure rolling wheel on flat ground, velocity = 0, BUT acceleration = omega^2 R UPWARD (not zero!).

solvedExamples.question: A uniform solid sphere (M, R) without initial spin is pushed with COM velocity v_0 along rough horizontal floor. Find final pure-rolling velocity v_f.
steps: Friction passes right through ground line => zero torque about ground contact point P!
L_i = M v_0 R + 0 = L_f = M v_f R + (2/5) M R^2 (v_f / R) = (7/5) M v_f R.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Trying F = ma + torque equations wastes 4 minutes; ground angular momentum solves it in 10 seconds!

weightageNote: Weightage: 3-5% IIT Exclusive Thermal & Acoustic Module (Carnot Efficiency, Entropy & Doppler Effect).

sections.heading: Carnot Engine, Refrigerator & Clausius Entropy
sections.summary: No heat engine operating between two temperatures T_H and T_C can exceed reversible Carnot efficiency eta = 1 - T_C / T_H.
keyPoints: Carnot Cycle: Isothermal expansion (T_H) -> Adiabatic expansion -> Isothermal compression (T_C) -> Adiabatic compression.
Refrigerator / Heat Pump: COP_fridge = Q_C / W = T_C / (T_H - T_C); COP_pump = Q_H / W = 1 + COP_fridge = T_H / (T_H - T_C).
Ideal gas Entropy change: Delta S = n C_v ln(T2/T1) + n R ln(V2/V1). For any cyclic process Delta S_system = 0; for irreversible process Delta S_universe > 0.

sections.heading: Doppler Effect in Sound & Moving Reflectors
sections.summary: Observed frequency shifts when source and/or listener move relative to the air medium.
keyPoints: General formula: f' = f_0 * (v + v_m +/- v_L) / (v + v_m -/+ v_S), where numerator uses + for observer approaching source, denominator uses - for source approaching observer.
Moving reflector wall (speed u toward stationary source): treat wall first as moving listener, then re-emitting as moving source -> f'' = f_0 * (v + u) / (v - u).
Transverse Doppler (radial v_cos = 0) yields zero classical shift!

formulas.note: Lowering T_C by dT raises eta MORE than raising T_H by equal dT
Always positive because AM > GM
For car approaching cliff at u with horn f_0

traps: Wind speed w simply shifts effective sound speed v -> v + w (along sound propagation direction from source to observer)!
Always take component of v_S and v_L ALONG the line joining instantaneous source-to-observer positions.

solvedExamples.question: A car approaches a cliff at 20 m/s sounding a 620 Hz horn (v_sound = 330 m/s). Find beat frequency heard by driver between direct sound and echo.
steps: Echo frequency received back by car = f_0 (v + u)/(v - u) = 620 x (350 / 310) = 700 Hz.
Direct horn heard by driver traveling WITH source = 620 Hz.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Applying shift only once (350/330 or 330/310) halves the true Doppler shift!

weightageNote: Weightage: 4-5% IIT Exclusive Electromagnetism & Interference Extensions (Cavity Superposition, Potentiometer & Thin Film).

sections.heading: Uniform Cavity Superposition (Electrostatic & Magnetic)
sections.summary: Treating a cavity inside uniform rho or current density J as superposition of full positive cylinder/sphere + equal negative cavity distribution yields exact closed-form uniform fields.
keyPoints: Uniform charge sphere (rho) with spherical cavity (vector OC = d): inside cavity E = (rho * d) / (3 eps_0), completely uniform in magnitude and direction!
Uniform current cylinder (J) with cylindrical hole (offset d): inside hole B = (mu_0 / 2) (J x d), uniform perpendicular to J and d.
Dielectric slab partially pulled into capacitor (fixed V): inward pulling force F = (1/2) (dC/dx) V^2 = eps_0 b (K - 1) V^2 / (2 d).

sections.heading: Potentiometer Sensitivity & Thin-Film Interference
sections.summary: Potentiometer acts as an ideal infinite-resistance voltmeter at null point, drawing zero test-cell current.
keyPoints: Potential gradient k = V_wire / L. Internal resistance r = R * (l1 - l2) / l2.
Lowering gradient k (longer wire or higher series R) improves sensitivity and precision.
Thin film (thickness t, mu) in air: reflection from air->film undergoes pi phase shift while film->air has 0 shift => constructive interference at 2 mu t cos(r) = (2n - 1) lambda / 2.

formulas.note: Strictly constant everywhere inside cavity regardless of cavity radius!
l1 = open-circuit null length; l2 = shunted by R
Minimum thickness t_min = lambda / (4 mu)

traps: Always check BOTH top AND bottom refractive index transitions before deciding whether thin-film bright reflection uses (n - 1/2) lambda or n lambda!
At potentiometer null balance, series resistance placed inside the SECONDARY cell branch causes ZERO shift in null length because I_branch = 0!

solvedExamples.question: Solid insulating sphere (rho = 3 eps_0 C/m^3) has spherical cavity centered at d = 2 m from sphere centre. Find electric field inside cavity.
steps: Superpose +rho full sphere and -rho cavity sphere: E_cavity = rho * d / (3 eps_0).
Substitute rho = 3 eps_0 and d = 2 => E = (3 eps_0 x 2) / (3 eps_0) = 2 N/C.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Radius R of the main sphere and radius a of the cavity do NOT appear in the uniform cavity field!
